subject: math
intro: I'm Ms. Chen. Systems of equations can feel abstract, so let's plan a lesson where the solution means something.

beats.narration: The solution to a system is where two things meet, so the title asks that.
beats.text: When Do They Meet? Systems of Equations

beats.narration: This standard covers solving systems of two linear equations, starting with graphing.
Graphing first builds the visual meaning before algebraic methods.
beats.text: Students will be able to solve a system of two linear equations by graphing and interpret the point of intersection in context.

beats.narration: The honest answer is "it depends," which leads straight to the intersection.
beats.text: Two gyms: Gym A costs $30/month; Gym B costs $50 to join plus $20/month. "Which is the better deal?" Students vote and explain.

beats.narration: Interpreting the regions on each side of the intersection is where students really get it.
beats.text: Graph both plans on one grid. Find where they intersect at (5, 150) and interpret: after 5 months, both cost $150. Discuss what happens before and after that point.

beats.narration: Writing a recommendation requires them to explain the intersection in plain words.
beats.text: Groups solve three "which is the better deal" scenarios by graphing and write a recommendation for a customer.

beats.narration: Checking in both equations reinforces what a solution to a system means.
beats.text: Graph y = 2x + 1 and y = −x + 7. What is the solution? Check it in both equations.

outro: A real decision, a graph, and a recommendation. Now plan yours.
